title: epan: Show a packet's process as frame.process fields
description:
Third of the series adding capture-time process attribution (design on wireshark-dev: https://lists.wireshark.org/archives/wireshark-dev/202609/msg00002.html; see #17525 and #1184; previous MRs: !26470 and !26471).

!26470 showed the process and thread ID from the standard `epb_processid_threadid` option, and !26471 gave wiretap a per-file table of process information blocks (Wireshark custom blocks and Apple's Darwin blocks). This MR joins the two: the process ID of a packet is looked up in that table and what the block says about the process is shown, generated, under "Process information" in the Frame tree.

**What changes**

- `packet-frame.c`: `frame.process.name`, `.path`, `.cmdline` (arguments separated by spaces), `.ppid`, `.uid`, `.user`, `.uuid` (FT_GUID) and `.start_time`, all generated, next to the `.pid` and `.tid` from the option. The user the process runs as fills `pinfo->user_name`, so the "User name" column works for captures with process information, as it does for Procmon files. A "Process" conversation filter (`frame.process.pid == N`) is registered, for packets only, so it appears in the conversation filter menus. The lookup runs whether or not the frame tree is built, since the column and the filter need it.
- `wiretap`: `wtap_file_find_pib()` looks a process ID up in the table through an index kept beside it (a hash from process ID to the block numbers with that ID, in file order). When an ID was reused, the most recent block whose `pib_starttime` is not after the packet's time stamp wins; blocks without start times fall back to the most recent one, and if every block started after the packet (clocks disagree) the first one is used.
- `epan`: the packet provider gets `find_process_info` and getters for the path, command line, parent process ID, user ID, user name and start time, in the style of the existing `get_process_id/name/uuid`; `file_packet_provider.c` implements them and Wireshark, TShark and sharkd supply them. The other front ends keep NULLs.
- `packet-darwin.c`: `frame.darwin.process_info.epid` and `.epname` were registered but never added to the tree; they are now added when the effective process differs from the process. A block with no name now still yields the process ID field, and the summary no longer repeats the process ID as the effective one when they are equal (it used to show `mDNSResponder(501) [501]`).
- Release notes: a feature entry.

**Tests**

`_gen_process_info_blocks.py` gains a third file, `process_info_pid_reuse.pcapng`, with two blocks for one process ID with different start times, two for another ID without start times, and packets before, between and after the start times, plus one extra Darwin packet with an effective process. `TestDissectPcapngProcessInformation` checks all the fields against the !26471 capture (including a block with only a process ID and one in a big-endian section), the "User name" column via the column format preference, the process-ID-reuse matching, and the Darwin effective process fields. The !26471 file-format tests still pass with the regenerated Darwin capture.

Built and tested on Windows (MSVC, Ninja, tshark-only build); suite_dissection, suite_fileformats, suite_mergecap, suite_io and suite_outputformats pass.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01MeQMmftoMWrDyC8HdFk7sT

+class TestDissectPcapngProcessInformation:
+    '''Process information from the pcapng process information blocks of a
+    file, looked up by the process ID in the epb_processid_threadid option,
+    as frame.process fields.
+
+    The captures are generated by test/captures/_gen_process_info_blocks.py.
+    '''
+
+    def test_frame_process_info_fields(self, assert_frames_match):
+        assert_frames_match('process_info_wireshark_cb.pcapng', [
+            (1, 'frame.process.pid == 1234 && frame.process.name == "curl"'
+                ' && frame.process.path == "/usr/bin/curl"'
+                ' && frame.process.cmdline == "curl https://example.com/"'
+                ' && frame.process.ppid == 1 && frame.process.uid == 1000'
+                ' && frame.process.user == "alice"'
+                ' && frame.process.uuid == 6b8b4567-327b-23c6-643c-986966334873'
+                ' && frame.process.start_time == "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"'),
+            # A block with nothing but a process ID.
+            (3, 'frame.process.pid == 4321 && !frame.process.name && !frame.process.uid'),
+            # A block in a big-endian section.
+            (4, 'frame.process.pid == 77 && frame.process.name == "sshd"'
+                ' && frame.process.uid == 0 && !frame.process.user'),
+        ])
+
+    def test_frame_process_info_user_name_column(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''The user the process runs as fills the user name column, even
+        when no protocol tree is built.'''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark,
+                '-r', capture_file('process_info_wireshark_cb.pcapng'),
+                '-o', 'gui.column.format:"No.","%m","User","%U"',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert [line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()] == [['1', 'alice'], ['2'], ['3'], ['4']]
+
+    def test_frame_process_info_pid_reuse(self, assert_frames_match):
+        '''With several blocks for one process ID, the start times and
+        the time stamp of the packet decide which one it is matched with.'''
+        assert_frames_match('process_info_pid_reuse.pcapng', [
+            (1, 'frame.process.name == "first"'),
+            (2, 'frame.process.name == "second"'),
+            (3, 'frame.process.name == "first"'),
+            (4, 'frame.process.name == "new"'),
+            (5, 'frame.process.pid == 700 && !frame.process.name'),
+        ])
+
+    def test_frame_darwin_effective_process(self, assert_frames_match):
+        '''The effective process of a Darwin packet is shown when it
+        differs from the process.'''
+        assert_frames_match('process_info_darwin_dpib.pcapng', [
+            (1, 'frame.darwin.process_info.pid == 501 && !frame.darwin.process_info.epid'),
+            (3, 'frame.darwin.process_info.pid == 501 && frame.darwin.process_info.epid == 1'

+ * @brief Finds the process information block for a process.
+ * @details Returns the ordinal number of the most recent process information

commits_data.title: epan: Show a packet's process as frame.process fields
commits_data.message:
epan: Show a packet's process as frame.process fields

Look the process ID in the pcapng epb_processid_threadid option of a
packet up in the file's process information blocks, and show what they
say about the process under "Process information" in the Frame tree:
frame.process.name, .path, .cmdline, .ppid, .uid, .user, .uuid and
.start_time, all generated. Set the user name column from the user the
process runs as, and add a "Process" conversation filter, which filters
on the process ID.

Index the process information blocks by process ID in wiretap, where the
table lives, as wtap_file_find_pib(); when a process ID was reused, the
start times in the blocks and the time stamp of the packet decide which
block a packet is matched with. Extend the packet provider with getters
for the new attributes and with the lookup, and supply them in
Wireshark, TShark and sharkd.

Also add the effective process ID and name of a Darwin packet to the
tree, as frame.darwin.process_info.epid and .epname, which were
registered but never populated, show the process ID when the block has
no name, and don't repeat the process ID as the effective process ID
when they are the same.

Add tests, with a generated capture for the reuse of a process ID.

Related to #1184 and #17525.
